cleared.result: Not retestable: bsc-rpc.publicnode.com, which reports reth-bsc/v0.1.4-hotfix-23b510f, now answers every historical eth_getLogs with HTTP 403 and 'Archive requests require a personal token', and bsc-dataseed1 answers 'limit exceeded'. No token was used. The only earlier result read through it is the BNB Chain row of Check 3 (tools/opdiff/swaps.py LOG_RPC, 8,326 swaps read newest first). A missing log cannot make that check pass falsely: the tick relation is checked per log, and a pair is two consecutive logged swaps with no logged liquidity change between them, so a missing Swap or ModifyLiquidity would give the second swap the wrong start price or liquidity and the pair would fail the single-step test. Every BNB pair matched, so the row stands; at worst it holds fewer swaps than it could. The BNB sync census of cycle 18 and this cycle select transactions from receipts of the head, not from that endpoint.

cleared.check: Which client produces Celo mainnet blocks today (L-877), from statements after the switch, header markers, and the block hashes reported by the two builds behind forno.
cleared.result: celo-reth. Celo Core Co announced on 22 July 2026 that mainnet is running op-reth (Celo's build is celo-reth). The decisive later statement is op-geth pull request 509, merged 18 August 2026: block 75,046,581 holds a CIP-64 transaction (index 29, 0xe9e0248c...) that celo-reth's fee rule accepts and op-geth's rejects; 'celo-reth nodes processed the block, op-geth nodes rejected it as a BAD BLOCK', 'the block is canonical', and 'the lenient rule is still live in the sequencer'. A sequencer that applies celo-reth's rule and not op-geth's is not op-geth. On chain, forno, Ankr and Pocket return that transaction in block 0x4791eb5 at index 0x1d, type 0x7b, fee currency 0x0e2a3e05..., gas 200,000 and maxFeePerGas 29,097,136,819 (product 5,819,427,363,800,000, as the pull request states); the sender's fee currency balance stated in the pull request was not reproduced, because balanceOf at the end of block 75,046,580 returns 2,136,764,000,000,000,000 and the balance at index 29 inside the block was not read. Headers carry no client marker: the last 40 blocks have extraData 0x0100000190000000050000002e90edd000 (the version 1 base fee parameters both clients write) and miner 0x4200...0011, with the same field set. The sequencer endpoint cel2-sequencer.celo.org answers web3_clientVersion with 'rpc method is not whitelisted'. forno answers from reth/v2.2.0-74cc8bb and from Geth/v0.1.0-untagged-c7ed55b8-20260817, the op-geth build of pull request 509's reviewed commit; the Geth backend is a follower, so the cycle 3 note that 'the sequencer RPC reports' op-geth c7ed55b8 described forno, not the sequencer. Of 200 heights (seed '42220-hashes', including 75,046,579 to 75,046,583 and 60 of the last 5,000 blocks), all 200 give one block hash across every build of forno, Ankr, Stakely, publicnode and Pocket; forno's Geth backend answered 196 of them and its reth backend 200. The clearances L-245, L-256 and L-343, which rest on block production by celo-reth, stand.

leads.question: Find a public BNB Chain archive endpoint without a token that serves eth_getLogs for windows older than about a day, and rerun gapcheck2.py on the ten cycle 18 windows there.
leads.why: The reth-bsc endpoint that once answered an old window with an empty list now refuses historical requests, so whether it still drops logs is unknown; only the Check 3 sample size depends on it.

leads.question: Any future census that selects transactions from receipts on Base or Avalanche must treat a null receipt as missing and read it elsewhere; the Pocket endpoints return null for receipts they do not hold.
leads.why: A census that took a null as 'no logs' would look complete without being so.

leads.question: op-geth pull request 509 says the fee currency exemption list may be incomplete while the sequencer keeps celo-reth's rule. Does forno's Geth backend, which serves reads, stall or diverge at a later such block, and does any public endpoint still answer from an op-geth that stopped at 75,046,581?
leads.why: A follower stuck on an old head would serve stale balances and pool state to users. It moves no PoolManager funds.

leadResults.answer: gapcheck2.py ran on HyperEVM (purroofgroup, hyperlend, official), Monad (rpc.monad.xyz, monadinfra), MegaETH, Tempo, Arc, Celo (forno), X Layer and Unichain, and on the unread windows of Base and Avalanche, with receipts from every endpoint and eth_getTransactionReceipt where eth_getBlockReceipts is missing. A known-block check on the census lists of HyperEVM, Monad, MegaETH and Unichain added 200 blocks that hold census transactions. No endpoint returned fewer logs than the receipts hold. The HyperEVM official endpoint refuses large windows loudly and Pocket on Base returns null receipts for some old blocks; neither returns a short log list. The one endpoint known to have done so (reth-bsc at publicnode) now refuses historical requests without a token; the only earlier result read through it is the BNB Chain row of Check 3, which a missing log cannot make pass. No result in OPCODES.md rests on an endpoint shown to drop logs.

celo-reth produces Celo blocks. op-geth pull request 509 (merged 18 August 2026) records that canonical block 75,046,581 was accepted by celo-reth and rejected by op-geth and that celo-reth's rule is still live in the sequencer; the forum post of 22 July 2026 says mainnet runs op-reth. Headers carry no client marker. 200 heights give the same hash from forno's reth and Geth backends and four other endpoints.

20 windows of 2,000 blocks from deployment to head: 10795 transactions, 14234 settles matching the transient model, none ending with an ERC-20 synced; transaction lists confirmed on a second endpoint.
12001 more BNB Chain transactions traced at the head, total 20717; no settle differs from the model and none ends with an ERC-20 synced.
